summary: Post-land P2s in services/desk-gateway, on main @ dcac9c0. desk_intake_ack delivers the origin reply at most once per ack: a write-ahead delivery marker in the intake record plus the same marker embedded in the comment body, so a store failure after a successful comment cannot buy a second comment on the retry (4141126604). desk_railway_status scopes latest_deployment to one environment — production when the project has one, else the single/first listed — names that environment, and _find_service returns that environment's deployment so railway_logs and the railway_redeploy staleness check both act on the environment they report (4141126611). Second commit answers the three Greptile P1s on the first: the recovery lookup carries a `since` window anchored to the first attempt so a thread longer than the page budget cannot strand the intake (4141224505); acks for the same reply are serialised per ack and re-read the record inside that lock, so two calls in flight together cannot both post (4141224477); and a lookup that cannot answer, an unconfigured gateway included, now refuses to advance rather than marking an intake acknowledged on the chance the reply landed (4141224494).

claims.claim: P2 4141126604: a successful GitHub comment followed by a failing Store.intake_ack leaves the intake un-advanced, and the retry that failure asks for advances the record without posting a second comment — asserted on the fake issue's comment list, which holds exactly one body

The same holds in the narrower window where even the delivery record could not be written: the retry reads the issue back, finds the marker it would have posted, and finishes the advance without posting. One comment, one lookup

An outcome that cannot be read back fails closed: with the comment lookup returning HTTP 403 the tool returns notify_unknown, posts nothing, and the intake stays claimed; once the lookup answers again the same call finishes with one comment still on the issue
Idempotence is per ack and not per intake: a later ack with a different status and message on the same intake posts its own reply, so the guard cannot swallow a reply the requester was owed

Store.intake_delivery is a write of its own, keyed per ack, and returns None for an unknown intake_id; the delivery state survives being re-read from disk. An `attempted` write keeps first_at from the first attempt, and a state meaning nothing was sent drops it so the next attempt is a first attempt again

Greptile P1 4141224505: the recovery lookup carries a `since` window anchored a day before the first attempt, so on an issue seeded with 600 older comments — past the lookup's 5x100 page budget — the retry still finds its marker on the first page and does not repost. Asserted on the query parameters the real GitHub.find_issue_comment sent

Greptile P1 4141224477: two desk_intake_ack calls for the same ack issued concurrently, with the POST held open 200ms to force the overlap, post exactly one comment; one reports posted:true and the other posted:false, and both report delivered:true

Greptile P1 4141224494: with an attempt recorded and the GitHub token then gone, the ack returns notify_unknown with notify.error not_configured, posts nothing, and leaves the intake claimed rather than advancing it. The carve-out for a reply that was never attempted on an unconfigured gateway is unchanged

Each of the three P1 fixes has its own negative control: removing the `since` window strands the intake at notify_unknown, removing the per-ack lock posts two identical comments, and restoring the not_configured early return advances the intake on an unreadable outcome

Both negative controls show these tests failing against the code on main @ dcac9c0, so they are keyed on the defects rather than merely green. The duplicate-comment assertion is the one that fires first

P2 4141126611: with a service deployed in staging (listed first) and production, railway_status reports latest_deployment as production's dep-prod and environment_id as env-prod, while deployments still carries both environments
railway_logs falls back to the chosen environment's deployment: it reads dep-prod, not the staging instance the API listed first, and reports the environment_id it read from
A service with nothing deployed in the chosen environment yields not_found naming that environment rather than another environment's logs, and an explicit deployment_id still reads whatever it names
With no environment named production the single/first listed environment is used, so a one-environment project is unchanged in behaviour
railway_redeploy compares prior_deployment_id to the target environment's deployment and redeploys into that same environment; the two pre-existing staleness tests are unchanged and still pass
The change is confined to services/desk-gateway and this receipt; ci/, ownership.yaml and other seats' paths are untouched, and the repo gate suite is green at this tip

unverified: No gateway was deployed or restarted; all evidence is from the unit suite in services/desk-gateway plus the repo gate scripts run locally

No upstream was contacted. GitHub is stubbed at the HTTP boundary, so the real comment_on_issue and find_issue_comment run against a fake that implements paging and the `since` filter as documented — but GitHub's own behaviour for those parameters on the issue-comments endpoint is not verified against the live API. In particular `since` is documented as filtering on last-updated time; if it behaved otherwise the recovery lookup's window would be wrong

The per-ack lock is process-local, matching the scope Store serialises its writes in. Two gateway processes sharing one data directory are outside what either guards; there the durable marker and the lookup are the only defence, and that configuration is untested

The recovery window is widened by 24h against clock skew between this gateway and GitHub. Skew larger than that would narrow the window past the comment and could produce a duplicate; no clock-skew scenario was tested

Delivery records written by the first commit of this branch carry no first_at, so a recovery lookup for one of those falls back to reading the thread from its start — the pre-fix behaviour. Only relevant to an intake acked between the two commits, which is no deployed gateway

find_issue_comment walks at most 5 pages of 100 comments within the `since` window. A window that somehow held more than 500 comments returns complete:false, which the ack treats as unknown and refuses to post on — correct but untested at that volume

The ack idempotency key is a digest of the ack arguments, so a retry that deliberately changes the message is a new delivery and posts again. That is the intended trade-off against suppressing a second legitimate reply; it is asserted for a different status, not for a reworded retry of the same status

Whether Railway can return service instances with no environments listed on the project is unknown; that case falls back to the single environment in deployments, and to no deployment when several are present
